reason: Both issues have identical titles, descriptions, and are reported by the same author; A is a clean recreation of B after B's discussion became sidetracked.
Both issues describe the exact same compilation error in Affine3 operator* with identical code and error messages; issue #8261 was reformatted into #8262.
Both issues describe identical CvVideoCamera crash on iOS 10 when repeatedly starting/stopping, with identical crash logs and reproduction code (robertofrontado's comment in B matches A exactly).
Both issues describe the identical feature request for dynamic CUDA plugin support in OpenCV DNN with the same technical approach, goals, and implementation details.
Both issues describe identical build failure on Mac OS X with same error at same file/line (window_QT.cpp:3364) regarding glXUseXFont, same root cause analysis about improper #ifdefs.

Issue A explicitly references issue B as having the exact same problem, shows identical error messages (CUDA_ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND 301 in CuvidVideoSource followed by Unsupported video source), and the same user (Dyex719) appears in both; the fix from B did not resolve A.

Both issues report identical crashes in cv::ocl::OpenCLAllocator::upload during cv::Mat::copyTo on RK3588 hardware with same OpenCV version, OS, compiler, multi-threading context, and week-long runtime before failure; stack traces and error locations match exactly.

Both issues report identical CANN graph check failures in compileCannGraph on Ascend310P3 hardware, with the same loadToDevice error; Issue B was fixed by correcting a hardcoded SoC version, but the problem reappears in OpenCV 4.9.0 (Issue A).
Both issues contain nearly identical optical flow tracking code with only different video URLs, indicating duplicate reports.
Both are arm64 NEON FP16 math operator accuracy test failures from the same commit, but in different test suites (MatMatTest vs MatScalarTest).
Both issues report the identical AttributeError for cv2.ximgproc.thinning missing in opencv-contrib-python 4.10.0.84, with same root cause and solutions.
Both issues describe identical MSER parameter transition problems from OpenCV 2.4 to 3, with issue B explicitly closed as a duplicate of issue A.
Both issues report the identical generator error 'unable to resolve base face::Facemark for face_FacemarkKazemi' when building OpenCV.js/WASM with the face module enabled.

Both issues describe the identical problem of CMake failing to find CUDNN on Windows when building OpenCV with CUDA, with the same error message and similar solutions (merging CUDNN into CUDA folder or manually setting CUDNN_LIBRARY/CUDNN_INCLUDE_DIR).
Issue B was closed by the same author to open a fresh issue (A) for the same unresolved problem of V4L2 MJPEG capture with VAAPI hardware acceleration.
Both issues report identical test failures when building OpenCV 4.10.0 with the same configuration (Ubuntu 24.04, GCC 13.2.0, ENABLE_FAST_MATH=ON) and identical cmake parameters.

Both issues involve inaccurate frame seeking with VideoCapture::set(CAP_PROP_POS_FRAMES) using the ffmpeg backend; Issue A references Issue B and the maintainer links them as discussions about the same property limitations.

Both issues concern inconsistent row/column vector representation in cv::InputArray for std::array types, but A focuses on std::array<cv::Mat,N> method conflicts while B covers std::array<float,N>, std::vector<float>, and float[] with Mat constructor conflicts.

Both issues report the identical 'memcpy was not declared in this scope' error at the same location in string.h on Ubuntu 16.04 with CUDA 7.5 during OpenCV CUDA compilation, indicating the same root cause despite different OpenCV versions.

Both issues involve OpenCV DNN failing to load PyTorch detection models (Mask R-CNN and Faster R-CNN) exported to ONNX due to unsupported dynamic shapes and post-processing operators like NMS/TopK, causing parsing errors in graph_simplifier.cpp.
Both issues report identical symptoms, reproduction steps, and environment regarding VideoCapture not raising exceptions immediately with setExceptionMode(True) on connection failure.
Both issues involve cv::resize and memory concerns, but differ in version (4.10.0 vs 2.4.9), platform, symptoms (gradual leak vs crash with invalid refcount), and resolution status.
Both issues concern forcing video codec in FFmpeg backend; B implemented global env var while A requests per-instance control.
Both issues show the same OpenCV DNN TensorFlow parsing error in tf_io.cpp:42, but involve different models (Mask R-CNN vs EAST) and usage patterns (writeTextGraph vs readNet).
Both issues describe CMake failing to detect cuDNN when building OpenCV with CUDA on Windows, with identical root cause and solutions.
Both issues concern CUDA support in OpenCV, but A focuses on version compatibility while B is an unspecified CUDA issue.

Both issues describe the same core problem: OpenCV DNN cannot load TensorFlow 2.x SavedModel directly, and attempts to convert to frozen graph fail due to TF2 eager constructs (StatefulPartitionedCall) and missing graph transforms.
Both issues report the identical assertion failure in findCirclesGrid at matmul.dispatch.cpp:439 in OpenCV 4.5.1, and issue B's fix (#19498) is confirmed to resolve the problem in issue A.
Both involve DNN CUDA backend failures but differ: A crashes on Windows during inference, B silently falls back to CPU on Linux due to missing BUILD_opencv_dnn=ON.
Both issues describe Homebrew ignoring the edited opencv.rb formula when building OpenCV with Java bindings (-DBUILD_opencv_java=ON) on macOS.
Both issues involve cv::norm SIMD integer overflow at type minimum values, but affect different norm types (L1 vs L2) and different kernels.

Both involve FileStorage incorrectly reading unsigned integer types (CV_64U vs CV_32U), but different root causes (strtoll clamping vs int casting) and different format scope (text-only vs all formats).
Both issues report the identical symptom: OpenCV stitcher silently produces a 158-byte result file instead of a proper panorama or error, from the same reporter in the same module.
Both issues concern the deprecated C API in OpenCV 3.x, but A is about missing version macros at compile time while B is about missing function symbols at link time.
Both involve -baseFormatSave legacy format but A is a usage error (LBP incompatible with old format) while B is a bug in XML output format for HAAR.
Both issues involve FileStorage YAML serialization failures where special string content (control characters vs whitespace-only) isn't properly escaped, but they are distinct bugs.
Both involve building OpenCV with CUDA 8.0 on Ubuntu 16.04, but A shows CUDA driver symbol errors (fatBinaryCtl) in cudacodec while B shows OpenMP/GOMP linking errors in video module.
Both concern medianBlur border handling, but A requests adding borderType parameter support while B (fixed) was about documenting existing BORDER_REPLICATE behavior.
Both issues describe the same nearest neighbor interpolation coordinate calculation error in OpenCV's resize function, with issue A explicitly referencing issue B as the same problem.
Both involve ORB detector crashes on Windows with heap corruption/access violations, but in different functions (computeKeyPoints vs computeOrbDescriptors) with different triggers and timeframes.

Both issues involve V4L2 pixel format unsupported errors in OpenCV's videoio module, but with different cameras (RealSense D435 vs Philips SPC 900NC) and different pixel formats (Z16 depth vs YU12 YUV), indicating distinct root causes in the same subsystem.
Both involve macOS framework build failures in build_framework.py, but A fails on opencv-onnx.pb.cc (dnn module) while B fails on stereobm.cpp (calib3d) with SSE4.1 errors; different root causes.

Both issues involve unsupported data types in OpenCV's DNN module when loading models, but they occur in different parsers (ONNX vs TensorFlow) and different source files (onnx_graph_simplifier.cpp vs tf_graph_simplifier.cpp).
Both issues describe PyCharm's inability to resolve cv2 references due to the module's binary extension structure and dynamic loading in __init__.py, with identical symptoms and root cause.

Both issues report missing implementations of SparseMatConstIterator decrement operators (prefix in A, postfix in B) in the same source file, with a maintainer explicitly noting B as a possible duplicate of A.

Both issues are VideoCapture crashes on Android 12 Samsung devices caused by MediaCodec decoder reporting frame dimensions (crop height) that don't match the actual allocated buffer size, leading to SIGSEGV when copying frame data; Issue A explicitly references #21149 as similar and the root cause is identical.
Both involve memory issues in SIFT detectAndCompute, but A shows gradual leak in a loop while B shows excessive allocation on a specific high-res image.

Both involve 'No module named cv2' on Ubuntu after building OpenCV, but A is a Python package path misconfiguration (site-packages vs dist-packages) in 4.6.0, while B is missing Python3 dev dependencies preventing bindings build in 3.x.
Both involve iOS framework build failures but with different root causes (objc bindings compilation error vs Python script bytes/string regex issue).

Both issues involve 'Inconsistent shape for ConcatLayer' errors in the DNN module, but A appears to be a user input size mismatch with an ONNX model while B was a confirmed slice layer bug in TensorFlow import fixed by PR #10748.
Both issues describe cv2.imread failing to read images when the file path contains German Umlaute (ä, ö, ü, Ä, Ö, Ü) on Windows.
Both issues describe the same memory leak caused by OpenCV's TLS data not being released when threads created via std::async terminate, with issue A explicitly referencing issue B.
Both are ONNX model import failures in OpenCV DNN module, but A lacks NonMaxSuppression operator support while B fails due to duplicate tensor names causing shape assertion.

Both issues involve CUDA build failures on Windows when compiling gpu_mat.cu in the core module, but with different OpenCV/CUDA/VS versions and error codes (MSB8066 vs MSB6006), suggesting similar symptom area but likely different root causes.
Both issues involve inability to set CAP_PROP_BUFFERSIZE, but A concerns FFmpeg/GStreamer backend for RTMP network streams while B concerns V4L2 backend for local cameras.

Both issues concern Mac Catalyst support in OpenCV's build scripts, but A is a specific build failure due to outdated compiler target (ios13.0-macabi) while B is a broader feature request for xcframework support to resolve architecture conflicts.
Both involve iOS framework build failures via build_framework.py but differ in error phase (CMake configure vs xcodebuild compile), OpenCV versions, and root causes.

Both issues involve fp16 ONNX models from onnxmltools failing in OpenCV DNN, but B was a missing FP16 support feature (fixed in #22337) while A is a new parsing bug with Resize nodes in a version that should support FP16.
Both issues report the identical AV1 decoding error caused by OpenCV's bundled GPL-free FFmpeg lacking libdav1d support, just on different platforms (Linux vs Windows).

Both involve building OpenCV with CUDA on Windows and enabling OPENCV_DNN_CUDA, but A is a build failure due to CUDA 10.2 not supporting RTX 3090 (compute capability 8.6) while B was a CMake configuration error from not enabling WITH_CUDA.

Both issues involve build failures at the opencv_cudafilters stage with CUDA, but A shows specific TIFF linker errors due to conda conflict while B suggests a parallel build issue with no detailed error.
Both involve incorrect FPS reporting on Windows but differ in scenario (live camera setting vs video file reading) and likely code paths (cap_dshow.cpp vs MSMF/FFMPEG backend).

Both issues propose identical enhancements for LLM inference in OpenCV DNN (dynamic memory allocation, KV caching, PagedAttention) referencing the same GSoC 2025 idea; Issue B is the completed implementation plan for what Issue A proposes.
Both issues report the exact same misaligned memory access bug in v_lut_pairs() at intrin_sse.hpp:3080 triggered by cv::resize() with odd byte offsets.

Both issues involve protobuf compatibility problems in OpenCV's dnn module related to caffe protobuf files, but they affect different versions (5 vs 4.7) with distinct root causes: stale generated files after Caffe removal vs C++ standard incompatibility with protobuf 3.x.

Issue A describes a broader 5.x inconsistency in warpAffine INTER_NEAREST across data types (new kernels vs old invoker), which includes the IPP mismatch from Issue B (fixed in 4.x via #29554 but not yet merged to 5.x).

Both are CUDA build failures on macOS caused by compiler detection issues with clang, but they show different error symptoms (missing string.h vs unsupported -dumpspecs option) across different OpenCV versions.
Both are compilation errors in hal_internal.cpp involving complex number handling in BLAS/LAPACK gemm calls, but B was fixed in 2016 while A appears later as a similar issue in the same code area.

Both are OpenCV CUDA build failures but with different root causes: Issue A shows specific GCC intrinsic errors (__builtin_ia32_monitorx/mwaitx) on OpenCV 4.2.0, while Issue B is a generic make failure on OpenCV 3.1 linked to CUDA 8.0 API incompatibility.
Both issues show 'Input layer not found' errors in TensorFlow importer when loading frozen graphs, but involve different unsupported layers (LSTM vs ROI pooling) and model architectures.

Different assertion errors in different functions (populateNet vs addConstNodes) with different root causes: Issue A involves unsupported TF ops (Range, Tile) causing CV_32FC1 type failure, while Issue B was a const_layers insertion assertion with various unrelated causes.
Both involve MSMF backend memory leaks in VideoCapture on Windows, but A is triggered by hardware acceleration during normal capture/write, while B is triggered by repeated open/close cycles.
Both are 'Input layer not found' errors in TFImporter::connect when loading custom TensorFlow frozen graphs, but involve different unsupported ops (Conv2DTranspose vs ROI/split).

Both issues report the identical assertion failure in TextDetectionModel_DB_Impl::unclip at model.cpp:1216 when using the model in concurrent contexts (Python threading, Java Singleton), confirming the same thread-safety bug.

Issue A is a Python bindings compilation error in GAPI module (GInferOutputs, GCompiloid), while Issue B is a missing header in samples/gpu (xfeatures2d/cuda.hpp); different modules, errors, and OpenCV versions.
Both involve iOS framework build failures but with different root causes (arm64 simulator support vs CMake/Xcode 10 compatibility).
Issue A is a missing header (aruco_detector.hpp) when building with opencv_contrib, while Issue B is a zlib compilation error due to missing unistd.h on older iOS SDKs.
Both involve GStreamer backend issues with VideoWriter/VideoCapture but different symptoms (linking failure vs pipeline hang) and platforms.
Issue A is about FindCUDA deprecation in CMake 3.25 when using OpenCV via find_package, while Issue B is about a stale CMake cache during OpenCV's own build with CUDA in 2017.
Both involve ONNX import failures in getMemoryShapes with inputs.size() assertion, but A is a ReduceLayer dynamic shape limitation while B appears to be a model export/layer-specific issue.

Both involve iOS build failures with 'Compiler doesn't support baseline optimization flags' in OpenCVCompilerOptimizations.cmake, but Issue B (OpenCV 3.x, armv7/NEON) was fixed in 3.4.0 while Issue A (OpenCV 4.x, arm64/x86_64 simulator vs device) is a separate regression with newer toolchains.

Both are iOS framework build failures using build_framework.py, but Issue A fails at CMake configuration with CheckTypeSize try_compile errors in libjpeg-turbo, while Issue B failed at compilation with a missing generated OpenCL kernel file, fixed by upgrading CMake.
Issue A is an off-by-one error in ROI calculation for zero-distortion case, while Issue B is about extreme distortion causing negative ROIs that clamp to zero.
Both issues involve findCirclesGrid failing to detect grid patterns (asymmetric with perspective distortion vs rotated symmetric), and a proposed fix for A would also address B.
Issue A is a genuine bug where cv2.dnn.DictValue is missing during import in OpenCV 4.8+, while Issue B was a user typo (readNetFromCAFFE vs readNetFromCaffe) in OpenCV 3.2.
Both issues are the same 'No CUDA support' error caused by incorrect CUDA_ARCH_BIN/PTX settings not matching the GPU's compute capability.
Both involve Reshape layer assertion failures in computeShapeByReshapeMask but with different assertion conditions (maskTotal vs dstTotal).

Both involve chessboard corner detection in calib3d, but A concerns regression in findChessboardCorners (regular) while B concerns findChessboardCornersSB (SB variant) with different symptoms and root causes.

Both involve cv2.fisheye.calibrate() array shape handling, but B was a 3.2 binding issue requiring (N,1,3) shape, while A is a 5.0 core regression rejecting that previously-working shape due to 0d/1d Mat changes.
Both issues are identical feature requests for λ-connected segmentation with the same description, motivation, API sketch, and references.

Both issues describe the identical crash in BundleAdjusterRay::calcError where negative focal lengths cause sqrt(f1*f2) to become NaN, leading to SVD failure; issue A explicitly references issue B as the same unresolved bug.
Both issues are caused by the same PR #27265 changing remap to float arithmetic, causing accuracy test failures on RISC-V RVV.
Both issues report identical warpAffine assertion failure with same 11176x226776 CV_8UC1 matrix dimensions and integer overflow cause.
Both issues are identical requests about enabling EXR support via OPENCV_IO_ENABLE_OPENEXR on Windows with prebuilt OpenCV and Visual Studio.

Both issues report CL_INVALID_WORK_GROUP_SIZE errors on Vivante GPUs (i.MX 8M) with identical root cause, affected kernels (including stage1_with_sobel), and proposed workarounds; maintainer explicitly links them as related.
Both issues report the identical GStreamer warning from the same function (isPipelinePlaying) in cap_gstreamer.cpp, indicating a common underlying issue in the GStreamer capture backend.
Both issues describe the same root cause: Mat.size.p initialized to point to rows field but used as array, causing intra-object overflow in different functions (setSize vs updateContinuityFlag).

Issue A is a cudacodec compilation error due to missing cudaVideoCodec_AV1 in CUDA 10.2's Video Codec SDK, while Issue B is a Python bindings generation error in the GAPI module caused by an in-source build configuration.
Both issues involve YoloV7 ONNX model crashes on Windows with OpenCV 4.7.0, but differ in backend (OpenVINO vs native) and build configuration (Release vs Debug).

Both issues concern solvePnPRansac and the useExtrinsicGuess parameter; Issue A reports a concrete bug where the initial guess is returned unchanged, while Issue B analyzes the implementation showing useExtrinsicGuess is ignored, explaining the root cause.

Both issues report that cv::cuda::resize (and its predecessor cv::gpu::resize) produces different results than cv::resize on CPU with INTER_LINEAR, and issue A explicitly references issue B as related.

Both issues concern cv::resize parameter handling (dsize vs fx/fy) but describe different problems: A is about ignored fine-tuning when sizes match, B is about inability to specify both parameters simultaneously.
Both request blending capabilities for drawing functions but address different aspects: transparency (alpha amount) vs blend modes (blending algorithms).
Issue A is a follow-up from the same SUSTech team referencing Issue B, asking about contributing custom layers after implementing the 3DSSD-based point cloud object detection planned in Issue B.

Both issues involve macOS framework build failures in the dnn module when compiling protobuf-generated .pb.cc files, but the specific failing files differ (tensorflow/versions.pb.cc vs onnx/opencv-onnx.pb.cc).
Both issues report the identical 'Camera index out of range' error from obsensor_uvc_stream_channel.cpp when using VideoCapture(1), and issue A is explicitly marked as a duplicate of issue B.

Both issues involve CharucoDetector.detectBoard() but A is a regression causing total detection failure under extreme perspective with cameraMatrix, while B concerns corner accuracy and pattern compatibility for calibration.

Both issues concern cv2.matchTemplate with TM_CCOEFF_NORMED, but A reports general numerical discrepancies between manual formula and OpenCV implementation, while B addresses a specific edge case (flat template causing division by zero).
Both issues show identical CMake error at OpenCVDetectCUDAUtils.cmake:297 from empty CUDA architecture list, and issue A's comment explicitly references issue B as the same problem.
Both request native batch overloads for different imgproc functions (resize vs remap) with similar API design, performance goals, and downstream use cases.
Both issues involve bugs in CommandLineParser but address different problems: negative value parsing vs. dash-only arguments and key syntax failures.
Both issues report that cv2.calcHist() Python bindings do not support non-uniform histograms with custom bin edges, showing the same core limitation.

Both issues involve OpenCVFindMKL.cmake failing to locate TBB libraries when MKL_WITH_TBB=ON due to changed directory structures in newer Intel MKL/TBB versions, but address different versions (2018 vs 2017) and slightly different path problems.
Both are OpenCL test failures on macOS with Intel iGPU fixed by disabling OpenCL, but involve different tests (Canny/SepFilter2D vs GaussianBlur/Morph/Resize) and different OS/hardware versions.
Both issues concern WINDOW_KEEPRATIO in highgui but on different backends (Qt/Linux vs win32) with different failure modes (regression after similar aspect ratio vs missing implementation).
Both issues involve OpenCV build failures on Apple platforms using build_framework.py, but target different platforms (iOS vs Mac Catalyst) with distinct CMake errors.

Both involve iOS framework build failures on Apple Silicon Macs with Xcode 14/Ventura, but Issue A fails during xcodebuild compilation for legacy architectures while Issue B fails during CMake configuration with contrib modules.
Both involve CUDA/CMake integration issues in OpenCV but differ: A is a generator expression error during OpenCV build, B is deprecated FindCUDA usage in OpenCVConfig.cmake for consumer projects.
Both involve GStreamer backend issues on Windows, but A is about plugin/DLL loading failures with explicit RTSP pipeline while B is about incorrect backend selection for webcam capture.

Both issues report cv2.fitEllipse failures on specific point configurations, with Issue A explicitly referencing Issue B as possibly related, suggesting a common underlying algorithmic weakness in ellipse fitting.

Both issues affect edgePreservingFilter(NORMCONV_FILTER) and stylization() in the same npr.hpp file, but A is a small-image edge case in compute_boxfilter while B is a large-image float precision bug in compute_NCfilter.
PR #7966 adds a check for all-zero Hu moments and returns DBL_MAX when only one shape has zero moments, preventing false perfect matches.
PR adds explicit validation for OPTFLOW_USE_INITIAL_FLOW flag with descriptive error when flow parameter is missing, directly addressing the issue.
The PR only conditionally links CoreImage for the highgui module, but the reported build failure occurs in the videoio module which still links CoreImage unconditionally.
PR fixes KMeans non-determinism with threads which likely causes flaky test, but issue remains open with failures spanning years suggesting possible other causes.
PR #9479 provides a workaround by moving MJPEG to end of probe list to hide warnings, but does not fix the underlying libjpeg issue; warnings still appear when MJPEG is explicitly selected.
PR claims to resolve the issue but it remains open with users reporting zoom still broken after camera rotation in later OpenCV versions.
The PR fixes the compiler detection for VS2017, resolving the main linking errors, but some compilation errors in performance tests remain.
PR improves vector conversion to NumPy arrays but doesn't confirm Keypoint/DMatch DataType specializations are implemented.
PR implements waitAny() for V4L backend only with different API (no GrabAnyEvent, GrabAnyItem, or grabAny function as proposed).

PR #30823 directly addresses the floating-point drift in solveLP() that caused infeasible solutions, adds a test for the exact issue (#12343), and demonstrates the fix resolves the reported constraint violations.
PR only fixes a typo (Scheimpfug -> Scheimpflug) mentioned in a comment, but does not address the main issue of renaming the rectification matrix or removing the extra parenthesis.
PR adds macOS installation guide but does not address package manager installation mentions or update outdated Linux instructions.
PR adds audio support only for Windows MSMF backend, not the requested cross-platform audioio module with ALSA support.
PR #16947 implements the exact fix proposed in the issue (saving convertFormat property) and is merged with 'resolves #16940'.
PR adds documentation pointing to existing release assets but does not provide new distribution channels like npm or direct download links as requested.
PR #29927 implements CV_64F support for patchNaNs in the 4.x branch, directly addressing the issue's request.
The PR updates the calib3d documentation to clarify the rational distortion model, distinguishing it from the Rational Function Model and referencing Brown-Conrady and division models as requested.
PR adds wrapped default constructor for ImageFeatures, initializing UMat properly and preventing segfault on empty descriptor access.
PR adds missing Python signatures for manually wrapped highgui functions including createTrackbar to the documentation generation pipeline.
PR B uses unique filenames via tempfile.mkstemp to prevent parallel test conflicts, directly addressing the sporadic file access errors in issue A.
PR splits static content but generated bindings remain in cv2.cpp, only a first step toward fixing memory issues.
PR #22164 fixes the angle discretization bug in HoughLines by changing cvRound to cvFloor+1, ensuring max_theta is reached, and includes a test for the reported issue.
PR updates filter2D documentation to include integer kernel support and adds comprehensive tests, resolving the documentation discrepancy.

PR #29077 homogenizes behavior by adding CV_Check input validation to throw exceptions for insufficient points in estimateAffine2D and related functions, matching findHomography's behavior as decided.
PR #30389 directly addresses the issue by adding empty checks before calling ptr() on map2 and dstmap2, and includes a regression test for the exact scenario described in issue #22763.
PR adds IMREAD_COLOR_RGB flag to read images as RGB but does not change the default BGR behavior, which was the core request.
PR fixes the shape_utils::total() int32 overflow but does not address the second int offset overflow in convolution_layer.cpp line 1841 mentioned in the issue.
PR skips the failing test as a workaround but doesn't fix the underlying cause of the sporadic timeout.
PR #30316 adds bounds checks for x2 in validateDisparity, preventing out-of-bounds access that caused crashes and unknown exceptions.

PR #28275 adds Doxygen documentation for getBlobContours() and collectContours but does not update sample code or broader documentation; issue comment confirms both #28275 and #29255 are needed to fully address the request.
PR #30727 explicitly fixes the overflow issue for ksize >= 257 by dispatching to a wider-counter implementation and adds a test that reproduces the original failure.

PR #30435 implements backend capability checks for specific capture modes and only emits warnings when the backend genuinely lacks support for the requested mode, resolving the false-positive warnings described in #26519.
PR #26559 explicitly fixes issue #26552 by updating ObjC/Swift constants to match core module definitions.
PR fixes the buffer overflow crash but the images still take over 10 minutes to process, indicating the hang issue persists.
PR #29714 eliminates the strict-aliasing violations and bogus C-casts by templating convexHull on the point type, removing the illegal pointer reinterpretations that caused the segfault.
PR fixes the crash by returning false instead of asserting, but camera still fails to open (graceful failure instead of crash).
PR #29878 adds test coverage for the zero-sized dimension case which exercises the false branch of _flatten_for_broadcast, addressing the missing test coverage mentioned in the issue.
PR #29425 removes stale Caffe protobuf files, moves generic helpers, fixes protobuf-free builds, and updates stub signatures, resolving all failure modes described in #29419.

PR #29493 implements the requested switch from LMUL=2 (m2) to LMUL=1 (m1) in intrin_rvv_scalable.hpp, with correctness verified on VLEN=256/1024 and performance data supporting the change; DNN kernel issues at VLEN=128 are acknowledged as follow-up work.

PR #30351 addresses all three issues: adds workaround() to free delayed Base64 sequence in release(), resets state to UNDEFINED in release()/releaseAndGetString(), and prevents popping root structure in endWriteStruct(); new tests pass with ASan/LSan clean.

PR B reorders distCoeffs unpacking to the standard (k1, k2, p1, p2, k3, ...) order, corrects the radial factor to the rational model, and fixes principal point handling, with a regression test confirming the fix matches the expected values from the issue.
PR clears stale initial flow buffers in prepareBuffers() and adds a test verifying the fix for both same-size and larger frames.
PR implements HEVC decoding for RPi5 but has unresolved CMake (HAVE_DRM) and runtime capture failures, plus missing tests/docs.

PR #29151 adds validation of raw maptype and ras_type values before casting to enum, exactly addressing the UBSan load-invalid-value UB described in issue #29150, and includes tests for the reported crash case.
PR B directly addresses issue #19648 by replacing GetTempFileNameA with GUID-based naming using CoCreateGuid, eliminating the race condition as proposed in the issue.
PR adds support for CV_8S and CV_32S but leaves 6 other unsupported depths (CV_16F, CV_16BF, CV_Bool, CV_64U, CV_64S, CV_32U) for a follow-up.
The PR adds documentation about passing None for outImg but does not change the API to make it a keyword argument as requested in the issue.
PR only updates documentation for patchNaNs type support while issue requests implementation of CV_64F support.
PR #29506 explicitly fixes issue #22093 by making isMaskSupported return false when crossCheck is enabled and modifying knnMatchImpl to drop the mask.
PR adds zlib-ng as optional alternative via WITH_ZLIB_NG, but doesn't replace zlib by default.
PR adds documentation and regression test for degenerate contours as agreed in issue discussion.
PR #18547 explicitly solves issue #18546 by adding Mat↔NSImage conversions for macOS/AppKit, which was the exact request in the issue.
PR enables filesystem support in OpenCV.js via Emscripten, directly addressing the issue.
PR adds missing return statement and CV_UNUSED macros to fix the compile error in ipp_warpAffine when IPP_IW is disabled.
The PR updates octree methods and creates a PCC API framework, addressing only the initial refactoring step of the issue's multi-stage plan.
PR skips the failing test instead of fixing the root cause.
PR fixes TM_CCOEFF_NORMED precision loss via double-precision integrals but does not address TM_CCOEFF method also reported in the issue.
PR implements core logging infrastructure (tag-based filtering, wildcard config, line info) but lacks full integration across modules and has incomplete startup configuration parsing.
PR disables the failing tests mentioned in the issue rather than fixing the underlying GStreamer MPEG encoding problem.
PR #29255 updates the sample code to demonstrate contour collection, addressing only the sample-code portion of #25904; the Doxygen documentation gap was fixed separately in #28275.
PR B implements the exact optimization suggested in issue A by replacing std::vector temporary allocations with stack arrays and AutoBuffer in TorchImporter::readTorchObject.
PR #29843 was merged and explicitly resolves issue #4269 by adding camera device enumeration API.
PR #21407 implements the weighted Hough transform feature requested in issue #4304 by adding a 'use_edgeval' parameter to accumulate pixel values as weights.
PR B explicitly fixes a race condition in the same test (PyrLKOpticalFlow.Mat) that caused sporadic failures in issue A.
PR B implements the exact fix proposed in issue A by updating outputVideoFormat when the output format is changed via properties.
The merged PR explicitly sets CMake policy CMP0072 to prefer legacy GL, which suppresses the warning reported in the issue.
PR implements CPU ColorHashTSDFVolume but GPU implementation remains outstanding as noted in both PR future work and issue comments.
PR B adds a ksize <= 255 guard in medianBlur dispatcher to route larger kernels to medianBlur_8u_Om, fixing the assertion failure for ksize >= 257 described in issue A.
PR #30072 directly addresses the teardown deadlock by preventing TBB arena/scheduler destruction during static teardown, validated by stress tests showing no deadlocks.
B only updates documentation for the affected functions but does not fix the code regression causing the throws.
PR B fixes a bug in stereo calibration when intrinsic guesses are provided, but does not implement the requested per-camera FIX_INTRINSICS feature from issue A.
PR B adds RANSAC parameters as function inputs to estimateRigidTransform, directly implementing the feature requested in issue A.
PR B addresses inliers in solvePnPRansac, which is the same function and area as issue A, but the exact changes are unknown.
PR #5484 explicitly fixes issue #4426 by correcting the assertion to accept the same input point formats as findFundamentalMat.
PR #26366 fixes the mask threshold inconsistency in ORB detector for masks with values 0 and 1, which is the exact issue described in #4574.
PR adds 16-bit support to fastNlMeansDenoising, fulfilling the main request of the issue.
B adds a new PnP algorithm but does not address the requested redesign, documentation, or testing improvements.

PR B explicitly adds CUDA::cudart target to all modules using CUDA, allowing opencv_core to be used independently and exposing cudart to consumers, directly resolving the linking failure described in issue A.
PR B implements the exact fix suggested in issue A, replacing the trunc(a+0.5) approach with wasm_f32x4_nearest for correct round-to-nearest ties-to-even behavior in v_round for WASM SIMD.
PR #14015 adds support for setting TIFF compression settings, which directly implements the requested ability to disable/enable LZW compression for TIFF writing.
PR #8044 explicitly mentions 'related #5012' and adds support for world build with contrib modules, addressing the same area but not necessarily fully fixing the specific linker error.
PR fixes rounding errors in flat regions for TM_CCOEFF_NORMED but doesn't explicitly resolve the mathematical undefined result for perfectly flat templates.
The PR adds IPPE method for planar pose estimation which solves the planar case in the issue, but does not fix the existing SOLVEPNP_ITERATIVE failure.
Both involve traincascade's -baseFormatSave option, but B fixes missing type_id for loading while A's error is about LBP incompatibility with old format.
PR B adds subsequence reading to imreadmulti but does not address the Python binding bug in issue A where imreadmulti returned an empty list; that bug was fixed by a separate patch (commit 2d34443).

PR implements only 2 of 6 proposed changes (explicit Estimator setting and Stitcher::create consolidation), leaving FeaturesFinder/Matcher removal, Python exposure, LevMarq update, and CUDA removal undone.
PR provides a workaround for the failing test but does not fix the underlying ORB descriptor non-determinism.
PR makes GpuMatND wrappable in InputArray/OutputArray, a prerequisite for DNN support, but does not implement blobFromImage, setInput, or forward for GpuMatND.
PR implements the license change from BSD to Apache 2 as discussed in the issue.
PR narrows the test exclusion to GCC 11.0-11.1 as a workaround, but doesn't fix the underlying compilation issue in the test code.
Both involve OpenJPEG JPEG2000 encoder but address different bugs (wrong pixel values vs small image encoding failure).
B updates OpenJPEG to 2.5.2, partially satisfying the tracking issue's goal of updating to at least 2.5.1, but the issue remains open until a later update to 2.5.3.
PR B fixes GStreamer backend audio playback and seeking issues that directly cause the Media.audio test failures in issue A.
PR B fixes corner return in detectAndDecode but does not add CODE128 barcode support requested in issue A.
PR #24893 adds in-place support for cartToPolar and polarToCart, removes the assertion, and includes tests, fully resolving the issue.
PR #24903 adds setters for downsampling threshold, detector scales, and gradient threshold, addressing all requested parameters to make BarcodeDetector resolution invariant via configuration.
PR adds CV_Bool mask support only in the 3d module, while the issue requests broader support across OpenCL, CUDA, HAL, and mask generators.
PR B directly fixes the memory leak in cvGetWindowRect_COCOA, which is the root cause of the issue reported in A.
PR #27443 implements the exact feature proposed in issue #27276, adding custom stream sources in Python for G-API with a C++ proxy class and Python factory function.
PR B fixes the dangling separator issue when LD_LIBRARY_PATH is unset but still mutates the environment, not fully addressing the core issue of unexpected modification.
PR fixes IPPICV unpack (issue 1) and IPPIW CMakeLists.txt copy (issue 2) but does not address FFMPEG copy failures (issue 3) or Qt qt_disable_unicode_defines (issue 4).
PR introduces boundingRect2f() as a new method for exact floating-point bounding rect, addressing the core need but not fixing the original boundingRect() method.
PR fixes MinGW DShow compilation but targets issue #17207 on 3.4 branch, not the reported issue #13549 on master.
PR adds only a tutorial for using opencv.js in Node.js, but does not create an npm package or address the build/distribution issues requested in the issue.
PR B adds OpenCL cross-check for float descriptors (CV_32FC1) only, not binary descriptors with Hamming distance as requested in issue A.
PR #25898 adds src==dst check in OpenCL warpTransform to clone source, fixing the in-place UMat WarpAffine bug reported in #25853.
Both PRs fix the exact same issue (#28036) by passing min_theta to OpenCL kernels and updating angle calculations in the same files (hough.cpp and hough_lines.cl).

Both PRs fix the exact same issue (#28036) with identical changes: passing min_theta to OpenCL kernels and correcting angle computation from theta*idx to min_theta+theta*idx in fill_accum_global, fill_accum_local, and get_lines kernels.
Both PRs fix the exact same issue (#28036) with identical core changes to pass min_theta to OpenCL HoughLines kernels; PR B adds extra validation and tests but is the same fundamental fix.
Both PRs fix the same issue (#29774) by excluding the Gaussian pre-filter's extrapolated border ring from the ECC template mask in findTransformECC.

Both PRs fix the same issue (#29816) by modifying Imgproc_WarpPerspective_Test.accuracy, but PR A adds a validation mask to exclude ill-conditioned pixels while PR B raises tolerance and documents quantization behavior.

PR A fixes documentation for initInverseRectificationMap matrix order, PR B adds a regression test for the same issue (#22262); they are companion changes addressing the same bug from different angles.
PR #30378 is explicitly a port of PR #30377 to the 5.x branch, making them sibling fixes for different release lines.
PR B is a port of PR A to the OpenCV 5.x branch; they implement the same HIP/ROCm backend for cv::cuda but target different release branches (4.x vs 5.x).
Both PRs implement a libcamera backend for OpenCV VideoCapture with nearly identical scope and purpose; they are competing implementations for the same feature.
Both PRs fix the identical DTrees crash by changing the default CVFolds from 10 to 0 in TreeParams, addressing the same root cause with the same solution.

Both PRs fix the identical bug in BackgroundSubtractorKNN where zero learning rate was ignored, address the same issue #24226, implement the same freeze logic for CPU and OpenCL paths, and add equivalent regression tests.
Both PRs address EPnP/P3P issues in calib3d but target different functions: A fixes solvePnPRansac for planar objects, B fixes solvePnP for exactly 4 points.

Both PRs fix precision issues in cv::multiply and cv::divide but for different type combinations: #30665 ensures CV_64F output is computed in 64-bit float, while #30767 adds exact 64-bit integer kernels for CV_64U/CV_64S inputs and outputs; the author of #30767 explicitly states it does not overlap with #30665.
